01 / THE DOUBLE HIT

ONE £1M GAIN. THREE DIFFERENT TAX BILLS.

FIRST THE RATE.
NOW THE LIMIT.

Quietly eroding our
hard-earned gains.Two rate rises. Now a planned cut to the lifetime limit.
Here’s what that can mean in pounds.

THE RATE RISES · ALREADY IN FORCE

10%→18%

+£80,000

Already added.

Tax on a fully qualifying £1m gain rose from £100,000 at 10% to £180,000 at 18%.

6 April 202510% → 14%

6 April 202614% → 18%

THE LIMIT CUT · ANNOUNCED FOR APRIL 2027

£1m→£500k

+£30,000

Another hit.

With only £500,000 eligible for BADR, the other £500,000 is taxed at 24% instead of 18% in this example.

The lifetime limit would be cut by 50%.

03 / “BUT WHAT ABOUT FOUNDERS’ RELIEF?”

£10M TURNOVER?
NO? THEN
YOU'RE OUT.

A new relief that many smaller businesses cannot use is no answer for the owners it leaves behind.

£10m

Minimum turnover in the accounting period before disposal.

15

Qualifying full-time employees. Directors, contractors and agency workers don’t count.

Under the proposed rules, both conditions must be met. There are further ownership conditions and two of three growth or R&D tests to satisfy.

Read the Treasury’s proposed criteria ↗

Founders’ Relief is a proposal under consultation. It is not a universal replacement for BADR.

THE TURNOVER THRESHOLD IN CONTEXT98.1%BELOW THE ENTRY BAR.

How many businesses
does £10 million leave behind?

98.1% of UK VAT/PAYE-registered company enterprises in the latest ONS data have turnover below £10m. That is 2,113,885 out of 2,155,400 in the ONS Company (including Building Society) category.

Only 1.9% meet the turnover threshold in this snapshot. They would still need to satisfy the other proposed conditions.

Check the ONS data ↗
What this statistic measures

Our calculation from ONS UK business: activity, size and location 2026, Table 15, UK row: 2,113,885 ÷ 2,155,400 × 100. The data cover VAT and/or PAYE-registered statistical enterprises in the Company (including Building Society) category, not every Companies House registration or every business legal form. Snapshot: 13 March 2026; most turnover relates to 2024/25, with some earlier data or estimates. Counts are rounded to multiples of five. This is not a forecast of turnover at disposal or a measure of overall relief eligibility.

04 / WHAT WE’RE ASKING FOR

RETHINK THE CUT.
RESPECT THE WORK.

This campaign supports entrepreneurship and fair taxation. We’re challenging repeated changes that undermine owners’ ability to plan.

01

Stop halving the lifetime limit.

Retain the £1m BADR limit instead of cutting it to £500,000.

02

Reconsider the rate increases.

Review the move from 10% to 18% and its impact on owners approaching a sale.

03

Protect people who planned ahead.

Provide fair transitional arrangements and hear from businesses excluded by the proposed Founders’ Relief thresholds.
